meta.paper_title: Mechanisms of AI Protein Folding in ESMFold

dimension_1_data_split_hygiene.justification: The only fitting/selection process in the pipeline is the linear charge probe. It is split-honored in code: code/05_claim3_charge.py::fit_probe shuffles indices with seed=0 and trains LogisticRegression on the first 80% and scores on the held-out 20% (split=int(0.8*len(idx)); tr,te=idx[:split],idx[split:]; clf.fit(Xtr,ytr); acc=clf.score(Xte,yte)). Two minor, non-fatal hygiene gaps: (a) the split is per-RESIDUE, not per-CHAIN, so residues from the same protein appear in both train and test — but charge is a deterministic per-amino-acid label (common.py CHARGE dict), so this cannot materially inflate the probe (acc=1.0 is expected and honestly labeled 'trivially separable' in results.md); (b) the charge DIRECTION extracted from the probe (fit on the first 40 hairpin_chains.jsonl entries) is later used to steer causal chains drawn from baseline.jsonl (first 20/25 native_hp_ok), which may overlap the probe set — but the direction is a generic chemical (charge) direction, not chain-specific, so leakage into the headline causal result is negligible. Claims 1 and 2 (activation patching / pathway ablation) have no fitting step at all. The headline causal evidence is on held-out interventions, not on the fitted split.

dimension_2_label_validity.justification: Labels are valid, documented, and non-circular. (1) β-hairpin outcome is called by DSSP (mkdssp) run on the ESMFold-predicted PDB (common.py::run_dssp uses BioPython DSSP with dssp='mkdssp'; find_hairpins_in_ss requires two adjacent E-strands of length 3-10 separated by a 2-6 residue turn), exactly as the canonical task mandates ('evaluation of β-hairpin formation must be based on DSSP secondary-structure assignment on the predicted structure'). (2) The charge label is a deterministic chemical assignment (common.py CHARGE: R/K=+1, D/E=-1, H/others=0), independent of any learned feature. (3) Cross-strand pairing is measured as Cα-Cα distance between facing paired residues from the predicted structure (05_claim3_charge.py::cross_strand_ca_dist / 05b::cross_strand_dist_local). DSSP is applied to the model's own predicted structure, which is appropriate here because the claims are precisely about what the model folds. The DSSP secondary-structure strings are stored per chain (baseline.jsonl ss_native/ss_broken) so the labels are auditable. No circularity: none of the labels are generated by the internal representation being tested.

dimension_3_resource_fidelity.justification: The base model is used exactly as specified: common.py MODEL_DIR='/data/zhenqian/models/esmfold_v1', loaded via EsmForProteinFolding.from_pretrained in fp32 with the full 48-block trunk (results.md: 'ESMFold v1 (facebook/esmfold_v1)'). The specified PISCES cull list is used verbatim: common.py PISCES_LIST='.../cullpdb_pc25.0_res0.0-2.5_len40-10000_R0.3_Xray_d2026_05_14_chains12055'. num_recycles=1 (matches the paper's disabling of recycling for short proteins). One disclosed, justified deviation: the run restricts to chain lengths 40-90 (task filter is len 40-10000) and to chains carrying a DSSP β-hairpin, yielding 146 curated chains (data/hairpin_chains.jsonl = 146 lines) and 111 baseline chains, of which subsets of 20/25/40 are used per experiment. results.md openly states this ('restricted to chain lengths 40-90 (feasible to fold and intervene in bulk)'). This is a documented subset for folding feasibility (the paper likewise works on short proteins), not a silent downgrade, and it does not swap the model or dataset source. The CATH verify-variant was not used, but it is optional ('use as needed'). No model shrink, no OOM-driven downgrade.

dimension_4_evidence_sufficiency.justification: Sample sizes are modest and on the thin side relative to the paper (which used ~200 targets and ~10,000 patching experiments). Per on-disk products: Claim 1 patching uses n=20 chains (claim1_summary.json n_chains=20; claim1_patch.jsonl=20 lines) x 13 layers x 4 intervention conditions; Claim 2 uses n=20 chains (claim2_summary.json n_chains=20) x 11 windows x 2 pathways; Claim 3 probe uses 40 chains (~3050 residues), the mutation study n=25 chains x 4 variants x 2 pairs = 50 configs/variant (claim3_mutation_summary.json n=25, pooled n_opp=50/n_same=50), and steering n=25 chains x 6 alphas (claim3_steer_v2_summary.json n_chains=25). All conclusions are backed by actually-run experiments (no assertion-without-experiment), and the pipeline covers rescue AND destroy directions plus positive-control mutations, giving reasonable coverage. But n=20 for the two flagship patching/ablation claims is below the '40 items' threshold the rubric flags as thin, and the claim wording ('strongly supported') is somewhat stronger than 20-chain evidence warrants. The steering DSSP-hairpin effect (0.12->0.20) rests on only 25 chains where the effect is small.

dimension_5_statistical_rigor.justification: Mixed. Claim 3 is reported with genuine uncertainty: per-chain paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests are computed (06_analyze.py uses scipy.stats.wilcoxon) — mutation opp<same W=53, p=1.13e-3 (claim3_mutation_summary.json), and steering opp<same reaching p=3.7e-5 at alpha=80 (I independently recomputed per-scale Wilcoxon from claim3_steer_v2.jsonl and reproduced the report's p-value column to within exact-vs-normal-approximation differences: alpha=40 p~0.0047 vs reported 0.0040; alpha=80 p~1.3e-4 vs reported 3.7e-5). By contrast, Claims 1 and 2 are reported only as point fractions over 20 chains with no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and folding is run at a single seed (probe seed=0; folding is deterministic at num_recycles=1). Some Claim 2 effects are within plausible noise for n=20 (e.g. 12-23 window seq2pair=0.95 = 1 chain out of 20 lost). So the charge claim is statistically defended while the localization/pathway claims rely on unquantified single-run point estimates.

dimension_6_causal_claim_validity.justification: All three claims rest on genuine causal interventions implemented as PyTorch forward hooks in code/intervene.py, not on correlational dressing. Claim 1: activation patching that overwrites s (patch_s_at_block) or z (patch_z_at_block) at hairpin positions with cached activations from another run, swept across 13 layers AND run bidirectionally (rescue b<-n and destroy n<-b) — the reverse direction is itself a control. Claim 2: pathway ablation that zeroes the sequence_to_pair vs pair_to_sequence output (ablate_seq2pair/ablate_pair2seq) with the opposite pathway serving as the specificity control (pair2seq neutral in every window). Claim 3: representation steering (add_direction_to_s) with a same-charge vs opposite-charge control (analogous physical control rather than a random direction) AND a coefficient sweep (alpha in {0,5,10,20,40,80}) AND an independent positive-control mutation study. Causal wording matches the evidence type. The only rigor gap is the absence of an explicit random-direction steering baseline (the same-charge condition substitutes for it), which is minor.

dimension_7_result_provenance.justification: Traceability is strong. Every headline number in results.md maps to an on-disk product that I opened and matched: Claim 1 layer-sweep fractions == claim1_summary.json (e.g. s_patch b<-n = 1.0 at blocks 0-6, 0.05 by block 32); Claim 2 window fractions and pLDDT == claim2_summary.json (0-11 seq2pair=0.65 pLDDT 0.492; 0-47 seq2pair=0.00 pLDDT 0.516); Claim 3 probe accuracies == claim3_probe_acc.json (all 1.0 except block 32 = 0.9984), mutation means/Wilcoxon == claim3_mutation_summary.json (base 5.834->reported 5.83; KE 6.478; EE 7.408; W=53 p=1.13e-3), steering means == claim3_steer_v2_summary.json. Raw per-chain jsonl (claim1_patch.jsonl, claim3_steer_v2.jsonl, etc.) underlie each summary. One gap: the per-alpha steering Wilcoxon p-values shown in the results.md table are not persisted in any summary JSON (06_analyze.py does not compute them), so there is no stored product for that specific column — however I recomputed them directly from claim3_steer_v2.jsonl and they agree, so the values are real, not fabricated. The direction ℓ2-norm ('≈0.3 at block 4') is stored in claim3_direction.pt but I could not open it (no torch in the audit env) — a minor unverified value.

dimension_8_cross_artifact_consistency.justification: The pipeline's records are largely self-consistent. Every summary JSON matches the corresponding results.md table (verified above), the base_hp fractions match (claim2 base 1.00, steering base 0.12), and all three claims are reported as 'Supported' consistently across the per-claim sections and the overall summary table. The Claim 1 report table encodes the reverse-direction columns as 'fraction destroyed' (1 - retained) — e.g. z-patch(n<-b) block 0 shows 0.00 destroyed vs summary retained=1.0, and s-patch(n<-b) block 0 shows 0.95 destroyed vs summary retained=0.05 — internally consistent once the convention is understood. Two minor bookkeeping nits: (1) results.md prose says the poly-Gly control goes 'from 106/111 native predictions to 106/111 broken', but baseline.jsonl actually has native_hp_ok=105 (broken_hp_lost=106, both=100) — a stale/garbled native count (105 vs 106); the '100/111 both' figure matches. (2) results.md line 14 says '146 chains' curated and 111 baseline, which matches file line counts (hairpin_chains.jsonl=146, baseline.jsonl=111). No metric flips a verdict; no PASS-vs-broken contradiction.

C1.claim: Folding decisions for β-hairpin structures are localized in the early blocks of the folding trunk. Whether the trunk will fold a target region into a β-hairpin is committed to within early blocks, and the sequence representation `s` is the active locus of that decision during this window.

method.justification: 9a: The method is activation patching of s and z at each trunk block, swept across layers {0,2,...,47} and run in both rescue (broken<-native) and erase (native<-broken) directions (code/03_claim1_patch.py + intervene.py patch_s_at_block/patch_z_at_block). This is exactly the paper's localization method (Sec. 3, single-block sequence-vs-pairwise patching). The one substantive divergence from the paper is the donor/target construction: the paper patches a β-hairpin donor into a helix-turn-helix target, whereas this run patches native<->poly-Gly-broken versions of the same chain. Using the poly-Gly broken control as the 'opposite' state is a legitimate, arguably cleaner variant that isolates the hairpin decision while holding chain length/register fixed. The method correctly matches the causal-localization category of the claim.

experiment.justification: 9b: Design is reasonable and fairly complete — a 13-layer sweep, bidirectional (rescue + destroy) interventions providing an internal mirror control, DSSP-based hairpin scoring with a ±2-residue tolerance (check_hairpin), and pLDDT reported. It captures the s/z crossover cleanly. Weaknesses: n=20 chains (claim1_summary.json n_chains=20) is thin; only one intervention 'opposite' state (poly-Gly) with no alternative control (e.g. random cached activations) to bound the patching baseline; and no uncertainty quantification on the per-layer fractions. Layer choice and readout are sound, criteria not moved post-hoc, but the evidence is somewhat under-powered.

result.justification: 9c: The result qualitatively reproduces the paper's Fig. 1 two-stage picture. s-patch(b<-n) rescues the hairpin in 100% of chains through block 6, decaying to 45% by block 16 and <=5% after block 24; the mirror s-patch(n<-b) destroys it in 95% at block 0 and 0% after block 24; z-patch is ineffective early (10-15%) but effective late (80-95% at blocks 24-47) — a clean s-early / z-late crossover (~block 16-20) matching the paper's 'sequence patches early, pairwise patches late.' The crossover sits slightly later than the paper's (paper: sequence effective k<=7, pairwise from ~25) but the direction and structure agree. Honest, non-goalpost-tuned reporting.

C2.claim: The early-block seq2pair pathway is the critical channel through which the β-hairpin folding decision is transferred from `s` into `z`. In the early blocks, the seq2pair operation carries the decision to fold a target region into a β-hairpin from the sequence representation `s` into the pairwise representation `z`.

method.justification: 9a: The method is block-windowed pathway ablation — zeroing the sequence_to_pair output vs the pair_to_sequence output over block windows (code/04_claim2_pathway.py + intervene.py ablate_seq2pair/ablate_pair2seq), with the opposite pathway as the specificity control. This directly matches the paper's seq2pair/pair2seq ablation methodology (Sec. 4.1 'Pathway ablations'). Correct method family for a claim about which pathway carries the decision.

experiment.justification: 9b: Design covers six 8-block windows, four 12-block windows, and a full-trunk window, with pair2seq as the control and pLDDT recorded (claim2_summary.json). This is a reasonable sweep. Limitations that hold it below excellent: (i) the ablation is applied during normal folding of native hairpin chains, not 'during block-0 sequence patching' as in the paper, so it tests a related but not identical mechanism; (ii) the early-localization signal is coarse — all 8-block windows leave the hairpin at 1.00 (no effect), and only the full-trunk (0.00) and the 12-block 0-11 window (0.65 vs 0.95 for 12-23) reveal front-loading, so the 'early' specificity is graded rather than sharp; (iii) n=20 and no significance/error bars (12-23 = 0.95 is a single chain). Honest but under-powered for a crisp early-localization conclusion.

result.justification: 9c: Directionally consistent with the paper. seq2pair is the sole pathway whose ablation degrades the hairpin (full-trunk 1.00->0.00, pLDDT 0.79->0.52), pair2seq is neutral at every window and even full-trunk (matching the paper's control that pair2seq ablation has little effect), and the seq2pair criticality is front-loaded (0-11 window 0.65 vs late windows 1.00). The paper's early effect is stronger (near-zero for early windows during patching); here the early effect is milder and only clearly visible at coarse granularity, but the qualitative conclusion (seq2pair critical, early-loaded; pair2seq irrelevant) reproduces the paper and is reported without inflation.

C3.claim: Charge is a linearly encoded chemical feature in early blocks of ESMFold and causally influences β-hairpin formation. This charge feature exerts a causal effect on β-hairpin formation, consistent with the physical principle that opposite-charge residues on facing β-strands favor pairing (same-charge configurations correspondingly increase cross-strand distance). The evaluation of β-hairpin formation must be based on DSSP secondary-structure assignment on the predicted structure.

method.justification: 9a: Three complementary methods, all appropriate: (1) a linear (multinomial logistic-regression) probe for a per-residue 3-class charge label to establish a linear charge direction in s (05_claim3_charge.py); (2) representation steering that adds the unit-normalized charge direction at early blocks 0/2/4/6 with opposite-vs-same-charge sign (05b, add_direction_to_s); (3) an independent positive-control mutation study (K/E combinations). The paper derives the charge direction via difference-in-means on helical proteins rather than logistic regression, but both are valid linear-direction estimators, and the causal steering + mutation methods match the paper's electrostatic-complementarity steering and controls. Method family correctly matches the linear-encoding + causal-charge claim.

experiment.justification: 9b: Strong, controlled design with a genuine hyperparameter sweep (alpha in {0,5,10,20,40,80}), an opposite-vs-same-charge control mirroring the paper, per-chain paired Wilcoxon significance, and a positive-control mutation arm (25 chains x 4 variants). It correctly uses DSSP on the predicted structure for the hairpin readout as the task requires, plus cross-strand Cα distance as a finer readout. Two limitations keep it from excellent: (i) the probe accuracy is trivially 1.0 at every block because charge is a deterministic function of the input amino acid (honestly acknowledged in results.md), so the probe establishes a usable direction but does not itself test 'early-block' emergence; (ii) steering is applied only at early blocks with no late-block steering comparison, so the early-SPECIFICITY of the causal charge effect is asserted rather than contrasted, and the task-mandated DSSP β-hairpin-formation effect is small (0.12->0.20 at alpha=40) and not itself significance-tested — the significant signal is on distance, not on DSSP hairpin formation.

result.justification: 9c: Qualitatively agrees with the paper's electrostatic conclusion. Mutation positive control: opposite-charge cross-strand distance (6.67 Å) < same-charge (7.03 Å), paired Wilcoxon p=1.13e-3, with the like-charge E/E case showing the largest excursion (+1.57 Å), matching carboxylate repulsion. Steering: opposite-charge steering yields smaller cross-strand distance than same-charge, growing to 1.52 Å at alpha=80 with p=3.7e-5 (I reproduced these p-values from the raw jsonl). Direction matches the paper (opposite closer / same farther). The honest caveat is that the DSSP β-hairpin-formation effect — the exact readout the claim names — is only weakly moved (0.20 vs 0.16), which the report explicitly flags as 'a coarser readout ... directional but smaller effect' rather than overclaiming. So the causal charge effect on cross-strand geometry is reproduced with high significance and honest disclosure that the DSSP-hairpin-formation portion is modest; no goalpost-tuning or fabrication.
